harvey-lab

Evidence & scope

Included after actual author, separate source-verifier and adversarial AI source-content reviews of exact approved bindings. Scope means the complete relevant available source documentation/methods actually recorded, with explicit bounded/unread pages, version differences and unknown rights, payload, construction or operations retained. No experiment, settled upstream rights, or human peer review is implied.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

harvey-lab · evaluates: The pinned Harvey evaluation document scopes each rubric criterion to its declared output files and asks an LLM to judge semantic satisfaction of match_criteria, without a separate golden reference output.

Permanent record ID: candidate.third11.harvey-lab.criteria.v3

  • The documented scorer fails a criterion without calling the judge when none of that criterion's scoped output files exist, or the run has no output at all. Each judge call uses the criterion-scoped outputs rather than all matter documents or all outputs.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

harvey-lab · evaluates: The captured Harvey methodology gives each judge a binary all-criteria-pass task score and averages the two default judges’ scores; dual task values can therefore be 0, 0.5 or 1, while strict aggregate all_pass requires both judges to all-pass.

Permanent record ID: candidate.third11.harvey-lab.dual-scoring.v2

  • The standard pair is Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-5.5. Pooled and macro criterion pass rates are diagnostics distinct from the headline averaged all-pass rate.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

harvey-lab · has stage: Harvey’s architecture document routes workspace tools through a per-task Podman container with network disabled, read-only source documents and a writable output overlay; the finish signal only checks that the agent’s listed deliverables exist.

Permanent record ID: candidate.third11.harvey-lab.isolation.v2

  • The finish existence check does not consult task.json and is separate from substantive rubric grading.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

harvey-lab · documents: The current Harvey evaluation document describes 2,010 tasks across 27 practice areas, while the earlier captured Mercor catalog describes 1,749 across 24; Harvey explicitly asks users to identify their release or commit because scores can change between releases.

Permanent record ID: candidate.third11.harvey-lab.release-scope.v2

  • The two rosters are preserved as source-version scopes; neither number is silently treated as a payload recount of the other.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

harvey-lab · benchmark task: Harvey LAB’s creator documentation defines a task as instructions, source documents, declared deliverables and inline criteria; the harness runs an agent on a synthetic matter file, evaluates its output and generates reports.

Permanent record ID: candidate.third11.harvey-lab.task-model.v2

  • The dataset and execution harness are separate components of the retained LAB family.
